Level surfaces of a gridded scalar field

Source: R/layers-stats-volumes.R
stat_isosurface_3d.Rd

Requires a complete rectilinear x/y/z grid with a numeric value aesthetic. Missing field values mask their incident cells. Coordinates are transformed before extraction.

Usage

stat_isosurface_3d(
  mapping = NULL,
  data = NULL,
  geom = GeomStatsSurface3D,
  position = "identity",
  ...,
  levels = NULL,
  caps = FALSE,
  method = "cubes",
  simplify = NULL,
  clip = NULL,
  na.rm = FALSE,
  show.legend = NA,
  inherit.aes = TRUE
)

geom_isosurface_3d(...)

Arguments

mapping, data, position, ..., na.rm, show.legend, inherit.aes

Standard layer arguments.

geom

Geom prototype for keyed triangle corners.

levels

Numeric scalar-field thresholds; NULL uses pretty levels.

caps

Whether to cap the sublevel region on the box faces (and on the clipping plane).

method

Extraction method: "cubes", "tetra", "dual" or "nets".

simplify

NULL, or a target face count (or fraction of the extracted faces) to which the surface is reduced by quadric edge collapse (mesh_decimate()). Normals are then recomputed from the decimated faces, or from fun in stat_isofunction_3d().

clip

NULL, or a plane made with sdf_plane(). The surface keeps the part on the side the plane normal points away from. With caps = TRUE the sublevel region is also closed on the plane, as with MATLAB's isocaps: each grid cell is split into the six tetrahedra of method = "tetra", the plane cuts each in a triangle or quad on which the linear interpolant of the field is linear, and the part of that polygon below the level is filled, as on the box faces. Plane caps point along the plane normal. The plane is in transformed position coordinates.

Details

method = "cubes" (the default) is marching cubes with the topology of the trilinear interpolant in each cell, as in Marching Cubes 33: faces whose corners alternate in sign are resolved by the asymptotic decider, and a bilinear slice test along each axis decides whether two boundary curves are joined by a tunnel through the cell. The cell triangulation is derived from these boundary curves rather than from a case table; curves of seven or more crossings are fanned around their mean point. method = "tetra" splits each cell into six tetrahedra around a fixed body diagonal and regularises the result (Treece et al. 1999): crossings closest to one grid point are merged where the merge keeps a 2-manifold, which removes most sliver triangles and the directional bias of the split. method = "dual" is dual contouring (Ju et al. 2002): one vertex per sign-changing cell placed at the minimiser of the quadratic error of the tangent planes at its edge crossings, so creases and corners of the level set are kept. The 3x3 normal equations are solved by an eigen-decomposition relative to the mass point of the crossings, eigenvalues below 1 % of the largest are truncated, and the vertex is clamped to its cell. Each grid edge crossing gives one quad between the four cells around it, split along the shorter diagonal. As in manifold dual contouring (Schaefer et al. 2007) a cell carries one vertex per level curve loop on its faces, resolved by the asymptotic decider, and a second level-curve arc between the same two vertices gets its own vertex, so the surface is a 2-manifold. method = "nets" uses the same connectivity with each vertex at the mean of its crossings (naive surface nets). Crossing normals for "dual" are interpolated finite-difference gradients of the grid, or central differences of fun in stat_isofunction_3d.

Field values within 64 machine epsilons of a threshold, relative to the maximum absolute field value or threshold, are snapped to that threshold. This gives shared grid vertices at numerically coincident intersections. Vertices are welded through per-layer edge arrays and all levels are extracted in one sweep over the grid. Finite-difference field gradients are interpolated and normalised at vertices (nx, ny, nz). Lighting uses the normalised mean of each face's vertex normals. caps = TRUE closes the sublevel region on the grid box with outward faces. Surface triangle winding points towards increasing field value.

Default levels are interior pretty(range(value), n = 10) values. The number of levels depends on the pretty spacing. level and z_mean are computed face attributes; .face, .corner and .vertex preserve triangle topology. A numeric fill aesthetic, a second field on the same grid, is interpolated trilinearly to the vertices, exactly on the grid edges where the vertices lie; with shading = "smooth" (see geom_surface_3d()) it stays per vertex and is interpolated across faces, otherwise each face takes the mean of its corners.

References

Lewiner, Lopes, Vieira and Tavares (2003). Efficient implementation of Marching Cubes' cases with topological guarantees. Journal of Graphics Tools 8, 1-15. doi:10.1080/10867651.2003.10487582

Nielson and Hamann (1991). The asymptotic decider: resolving the ambiguity in marching cubes. IEEE Visualization '91, 83-91. doi:10.1109/VISUAL.1991.175782

Treece, Prager and Gee (1999). Regularised marching tetrahedra: improved iso-surface extraction. Computers & Graphics 23, 583-598. doi:10.1016/S0097-8493(99)00076-X

Doi and Koide (1991), An Efficient Method of Triangulating Equi-Valued Surfaces by Using Tetrahedral Cells. IEICE E74-D, 214-224. https://globals.ieice.org/en_transactions/information/10.1587/e74-d_1_214/_p

Ju, Losasso, Schaefer and Warren (2002). Dual contouring of Hermite data. ACM Transactions on Graphics 21, 339-346. doi:10.1145/566654.566586

Schaefer, Ju and Warren (2007). Manifold dual contouring. IEEE Transactions on Visualization and Computer Graphics 13, 610-619. doi:10.1109/TVCG.2007.1012

Schroeder, Maynard and Geveci (2015). Flying edges: a high-performance scalable isocontouring algorithm. IEEE LDAV, 33-40. doi:10.1109/LDAV.2015.7348069

Examples

d <- expand.grid(x = seq(-1, 1, length.out = 10),
                 y = seq(-1, 1, length.out = 10), z = seq(-1, 1, length.out = 10))
d$value <- with(d, x^2 + y^2 + z^2)
ggplot2::ggplot(d, ggplot2::aes(x, y, z = z, value = value)) +
  geom_isosurface_3d(levels = 0.6) + coord_3d()
ggplot2::ggplot(d, ggplot2::aes(x, y, z = z, value = value)) +
  stat_isosurface_3d(levels = 0.6) + coord_3d()
ggplot2::ggplot(d, ggplot2::aes(x, y, z = z, value = value, fill = z)) +
  stat_isosurface_3d(levels = 0.6, shading = "smooth") + coord_3d()
